newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iraqi Kurdish groups sign ceasefire in Iran - paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurdish groups sign ceasefire in Iran - paper.

text.p: Two rival Iraqi Kurdish factions have signed an accord in Tehran to end recent clashes in northern Iraq, an Iranian newspaper said on Saturday.

"The Kurdistan Islamic Movement (KIM) and the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) wound up three days of talks on Thursday with an agreement for a permanent ceasefire, to free their captives from the other side and withdraw their forces to previous positions," the English-language Tehran Times said.
"The accord was signed by PUK leader Jalal Talabani and his KIM rival, Sheikh Abdul-Aziz," it said.
The PUK said on Monday it had clashed with the Islamic Movement in northern Iraq near the Iranian border last weekend as part of sporadic fighting that broke out earlier in April.
It said its traditional rival, the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), was supporting the Islamist group.
The KDP and PUK have met frequently for peace talks since they declared a ceasefire last October following intense fighting.
Kurdish rebels have been in control of northern Iraq since Baghdad's defeat in the 1991 Gulf War over Kuwait.
